Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the StellarTech Q1 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today's call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Janet Davies, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Janet Davies, VP of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and welcome to StellarTech’s earnings call. Joining me today are Robert Thompson, CEO; Susan Miller, CFO; and David Lee, Chief Technology Officer.
Earlier today, we published our earnings press release and slides, which are available on our IR site. Please note this call may contain forward-looking statements. Now, I’ll turn it over to Robert Thompson.

Robert Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Janet. Hello, everyone.

Let’s start with a look at the quarter:

We made strong progress this quarter. Our Q1 revenue reached $18.6 billion, exceeding our prior guidance of $17.5 billion by $1.1 billion, or approximately 6.3%. This performance was primarily fueled by exceptional strength in our Client Computing Group, coupled with encouraging signs of recovery in the enterprise and government segments of our Data Center Group.

We also saw great momentum in solidifying our customer relationships and ensuring supply chain resilience. We've successfully renegotiated or extended LTAs with three key customers this quarter. These include a 5-year extension securing 75% of AlphaTech Solutions' component needs, a renegotiated 3-year LTA with BetaCorp Industries focusing on automotive microcontrollers, and a new 7-year LTA with Gamma Global Electronics for memory chips.

These achievements underscore our commitment to disciplined execution and innovation.

Now I’ll pass it to Susan Miller to walk through in more detail.

Susan Miller, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Robert, and hello, everyone.

Let me take you through the financials:

First, building on what Robert said, we’ve continued to drive improvements in our customer relationships and supply chain stability. We've strengthened our relationships with key suppliers, including a new long-term agreement with a critical raw material supplier and investments in a new generation of lithography equipment. Our internal yield improvement programs have also been highly successful, reducing defect rates by 12% across several key product lines.

We invested strategically in improving our operational efficiency, which directly impacted our net margin and diluted EPS. We saw a reduction in our COGS as a percentage of revenue, dropping from 62% in Q1 of the previous year to 59% this quarter. This improvement was driven by supply chain efficiencies from "Project Streamline", manufacturing process improvements, and strategic sourcing initiatives. This boosted our net margin from 12% in Q1 of the prior year to 14.5% this quarter. Our Q1 EPS came in at $1.39, a significant $0.29 beat relative to our previous guidance. Consequently, we're revising our full-year EPS guidance upwards to $4.60.

Additionally, we’ve seen progress in reducing underutilization charges. These charges totaled $18 million, representing a 25% decrease compared to $24 million in Q2. This reduction is a direct result of our efforts to optimize production planning and secure new contracts. We are actively working to repurpose Fab A for the production of newer generation components, diversify our supply chain, and improve demand forecasting.

Now I’ll turn it over to David Lee, who will speak about operations and innovation.

David Lee, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, Susan.

Let me begin with a closer look at our revenue performance, particularly on the product side. Our Client Computing Group revenue stood at $11.2 billion, representing an impressive 8% year-over-year increase. This growth was underpinned by record notebook unit volumes, up 15% YoY, and a favorable product mix shift towards higher-margin premium notebooks. This was driven by the continued "Work/Learn-from-Home" trend, gaming segment momentum, and strategic partnerships. Data Center Group revenue came in at $5.6 billion, a 20% YoY decline, but an improvement over the 25% decline in Q4, signalling a bottoming out of this segment. We introduced "Project Sapphire Rapids", which introduced enhanced security features and AI acceleration capabilities, and it’s already contributing to renewed demand in the second half of the year.

I’d also like to expand on our sales guidance for the coming quarters. While overall PC demand remains exceptionally strong, we project CCG revenue for Q2 to be approximately $9.5 billion, reflecting a modest 3% year-over-year increase. This growth is constrained by ongoing industry-wide shortages of key components. The full-year CCG revenue forecast is revised to a range of $38 billion to $39 billion. We anticipate a revenue rebound in Q2 within our DCG, with projected revenue of $6.8 billion, representing a 6% increase sequentially from Q1. The full-year revenue forecast for DCG is in the range of $28 billion to $29 billion.

Let’s move to the Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
You mentioned strong improvements in customer LTAs and supply agreements. Can you talk more about the regional impact of these agreements?

Susan Miller:
Certainly. The Gamma Global Electronics LTA is a significant win for our Asian operations, where smartphone and server demand is rapidly growing. The AlphaTech Solutions LTA solidifies our position as a key supplier for the growing AI market in North America. The BetaCorp Industries renegotiation reflects the increasing importance of the automotive sector for our business in Europe.

Analyst 2:
Can you elaborate on the trajectory of your Data Center Group revenue and the impact of your strategic initiatives?

David Lee:
Sure. We expect a stronger second half for DCG, driven by renewed investment in cloud infrastructure, a rebound in enterprise spending, and government initiatives focused on AI and data analytics. Our full-year revenue forecast for DCG is in the range of $28 billion to $29 billion. We expect to see a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $7.8 billion, and a 17% increase in Q4 year-over-year to $8.5 billion. Our GPU-based servers and specialized processors are gaining traction in areas such as machine learning, deep learning, and data analytics. We anticipate significant growth in this sub-segment, contributing over $1 billion in revenue in 2024.

Analyst 3:
With regard to underutilization charges, how does the company plan to further mitigate these costs in the coming quarters?

Susan Miller:
We anticipate underutilization charges to further decrease in Q4, potentially to below $10 million, as the new supply agreements take full effect and new production lines come online. We are actively working to repurpose Fab A for the production of newer generation components, diversify our supply chain to reduce our reliance on any single supplier, and invest in improved demand forecasting tools to better predict future demand and optimize our production planning.

Closing

Robert Thompson:
Thank you all for joining us today. We're energized by the momentum we’re seeing and look forward to sharing continued progress next quarter.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes the call. You may now disconnect.
